title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the axiomatic 'analysis situs' (tame topology, second draft, June 1986). There is a set M of 'multistrata' (elementary tame cells or simplices, viewed abstractly) and a set F of 'figures of finite type'. Each has a face/subfigure order ≤ and a 'shadow' relation ≪, roughly 'is set-theoretically contained in'. The previous page also introduces a relation ≭. Each figure F has an underlying set of multistrata F̃ ⊂ M, and the map F ↦ F̃ is assumed injective. The previous page defines the shadow Omb(X) = {Y ∈ M | Y ≪ X} and the multishadow Multomb(F) = {Omb(X) | X ∈ F̃}. Grothendieck wants Multomb(F) to be a set-theoretic figure in M whose strata are the shadows of the multistrata of F.

This page:
(i) This gives a map (*) F → Fig(M), F ↦ Multomb(F).
(ii) The map is injective. Each X is recovered from Omb(X) as its greatest element for ≪. So F̃ is recovered from Multomb(F), and F is recovered from F̃.
(iii) (1.38) G ≤ F ⟺ Multomb(G) ≤ Multomb(F). The strata on the left are the Omb(Y), Y ∈ G̃; on the right the Omb(X), X ∈ F̃. The reason given is that if G ≤ F then G̃ is a closed (face-closed) subset of F̃. So the abstract poset of finite figures embeds, order-faithfully, into the concrete figures built on M.

19 June entry: Grothendieck abandons his intended geometric meaning of G ≪ F for figures, namely 'G is a subfigure of a subdivision of F'. Even in the simplicial case, where the combinatorial structure of the multistrata is that of a simplex, this looks unnatural. His example: tame simplices X, Y in some R^n, with Y ≪ X meaning containment of the underlying sets. That would presumably require (or imply) a subdivision of X in which Y is a multistratum, and the next page doubts that such existence should be imposed.

He therefore adopts, on the next page, AE4: G ≪ F iff every X ∈ G̃ satisfies X ≪ Y for some Y ∈ F̃. Thus ≪ on figures is derived from ≪ on multistrata. The whole structure (F, ≤, ≪) is then reconstructible from (M, ≤, ≪, ≭).

Purpose: an intrinsic, combinatorial axiomatization of 'tame' (modérée) geometry, as announced in Esquisse §5. It replaces topology by posets of strata plus a containment relation and avoids subdivision/Hauptvermutung issues.
errors: Injectivity uses that X is the unique greatest element of Omb(X) for ≪. This requires ≪ to be reflexive and antisymmetric on M (X ≪ Y and Y ≪ X ⇒ X = Y), which is not stated on this page.

(1.38) is called 'immédiat' but the converse direction (Multomb(G) ≤ Multomb(F) ⇒ G ≤ F) needs that ≤ among figures is detected by inclusion of underlying sets of multistrata as a closed subset. This is an axiom assumed (from the previous page: order on F̃ corresponds to inclusion of multishadows), not derived.

The heuristic that Y ⊂ X for tame simplices yields a subdivision of X with Y as a stratum holds in PL/linear and o-minimal settings only up to definable homeomorphism, not as a linear subdivision. Grothendieck is right to be wary of building this into the axioms.

ideas.what: Abstract figures (F, ≤, ≪) embedded order-faithfully into set-theoretic figures on the set of multistrata via F ↦ Multomb(F) (shadows of strata).
ideas.modern_name: Representation theorem for posets of cell/strata complexes; face-poset reconstruction; Stone-type representation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Face-poset reconstruction of regular CW complexes: Björner (1984), with earlier versions in combinatorial topology

ideas.what: Defining 'shadow' ≪ (set-theoretic containment) between strata as a primitive alongside the face order, so that tame geometry is axiomatized combinatorially without a topology.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / o-minimal-style frameworks; stratified spaces via posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimal structures, 1980s–1998); programmatic idea: Grothendieck, Esquisse d'un programme §5
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5, contains the program but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Rejecting 'G ≪ F iff G is a subfigure of a subdivision of F' in favour of the elementwise definition AE4 (each stratum of G lies in the shadow of some stratum of F).
ideas.modern_name: Avoiding Hauptvermutung/common-subdivision issues; triangulation compatible with definable subsets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Triangulation of definable sets compatible with finitely many subsets: Łojasiewicz, Hironaka, van den Dries

missed.claim: An axiomatic theory of tame figures in which everything is reconstructed from the data (M, ≤, ≪, ≭) on multistrata, with figures embedded via multishadows. It was never written up or developed into a theory comparable with o-minimality.
missed.quote: Finalement, j'ai changé de point de vue pour le sens géométrique de la relation G ≪ F, que je voulais comme "G est une sous-figure d'une subdivision de F".
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A purely order-theoretic axiomatization of tame geometry (strata plus containment) could be compared with o-minimal cell decomposition and with poset models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories). Such a comparison does not appear to have been made.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in an unpublished axiomatic of tame topology: an injectivity and order-embedding check plus a change of definition. It is interesting as documentation of the Esquisse §5 program, but the individual results are routine.
transcription_corrections: 'Multcomb' should read 'Multomb' (multiombre, as defined on p.19).
'Ouv(X)' / 'Ouvs(Y)' should read 'Omb(X)' / 'Ombs(Y)' (shadows), matching the definitions on p.19.
'partie finissante[?]' is more likely 'partie fermée' (face-closed subset) of F̃.
In (1.38) the equivalence arrow overwrites a crossed-out arrow (likely an implication changed to an equivalence).
'variété[?] modérée' is uncertain; the sense is 'a tame setting' ('on a une théorie modérée' is also possible).
